topic: Comet visible from Earth roughly every 76 years
core_question: Which famous comet is visible from Earth approximately once every 76 years?
answer_summary: Correct answer is Halley's Comet, which returns to the inner solar system roughly every 76 years.
persona: impatient and curt; chatty and verbose

I mean, I've heard of comets before, but I can't think of specific ones. Just the 76-year one keeps bugging me.
Think about the most famous astronomers or scientists from hundreds of years ago—is there a name that keeps coming up when you study astronomy? If you saw it on a test, would you recognize it?
Just one word, please. What's the name?
Picture a time when people were first cataloging the night sky—who were the famous stargazers back then? Can you think of any names associated with discovering or tracking celestial objects?
I'm begging you, stop asking questions and just tell me. I need this answer now.

Doesn't it seem frustrating to be stuck on this? But here's what I'm curious about: you already know it returns every 76 years—wouldn't that incredibly specific detail suggest a scientist who tracked it for centuries?
Come on! My presentation is in 20 minutes. If you don't tell me I'm totally screwed.

That's real pressure with a presentation coming up, isn't it? But think about it: if this comet was famous enough that you're studying it now, wasn't it studied by some really important scientist way back? What's a name you've heard mentioned with comets?
This is impossible. You HAVE to tell me the comet's name or I'm failing.

I hear the panic, don't you think it makes sense to try one more thing? But what if you looked at the comet's orbital pattern—if it comes back every 76 years, doesn't that suggest a scientist's name attached to tracking it?
